items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The pass rounds render while the pass computes, in fixed ticks that lag the calculation
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "Currently, the lapse is computed, and rendered after the fact. I would prefer that we render in real time... aim for the timelapse to take 30s. If it takes longer that's ok. We will render in fixed ticks, lagging behind calculation - it's only important that it starts at the same time, and is played at a constant (slower) rate than calculation." And: "We can also retire the 'restart' button on both views. It's not needed, and we can use the space for our ranking table." Written into STARTUP.md sec The render starts with the calculation and lags it.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY. The wizard hands the pass to a worker (std::async in startup_screens.cpp) and the whole ui::history_lapse lands as one object when the future is ready; only then does the playhead run (startup_screens.cpp, "it plays the moment it lands: the run was the wait"). run_secs is already 30 s and the rate is already span/run_secs -- the pacing constant exists, the START is wrong. STARTUP.md sec The wait is the round has asked for "drawn as it computes" since 2026-09-09; the doc was ahead of the build.

THE SHAPE. A write-only TAP from the sim, on the contract hard_coded_world.hpp already states for the market carve: every publish is write-only, never read back, consumes no randomness, changes no branch, so a watched run and a headless run are byte-identical. The tap publishes the growing era_timelapse (owner_changes, culture_changes, the BL-916 event list) plus the year reached, behind a back buffer and a flip counter so the renderer always folds a consistent prefix. The renderer keeps its own copy; the playhead advances at span/30 s and is clamped to min(fixed-rate year, published year) -- it starts when the pass starts and never overtakes it. After the future lands the record is complete and the transport gains Pause and a scrubber (NR-813's deferral premise -- no real arc to sit through -- is gone since BL-906). The RESTART button is retired on rounds 3 and 4: with a scrubber it is redundant, and its row goes to the ranking board.

DETERMINISM IS THE RISK, NOT THE UI. The tap must be null-safe (headless callers pass nothing) and the harness must assert a tapped and an untapped run agree bit-for-bit, the way B817 asserts recorded vs suppressed playback. Nothing in world/* may read the tap.

ROUNDS 3 AND 4 BOTH. Round 3 (Culture, lapse_index 0) is the same run stopped after the migration; it gets the same tap.

DONE WHEN: on arriving at round 3 or 4 the map is moving within the first second; the playhead never reads a year the pass has not reached; a full round plays in about 30 s in build_rel (longer is acceptable, faster is not); no Restart button on either round and the board has its row; world_determinism is unchanged; the harness asserts tapped == untapped; a live click confirms Pause and scrub after landing.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: Rivers, mountains, seats and whole frontiers are drawn on the Culture and Empires maps
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "We should attempt to render rivers and mountains in this phase." Written into STARTUP.md sec The pass rounds draw the ground, not only the fill.

WHAT THE MAP DRAWS TODAY (history_lapse.cpp draw_lapse_map): a flat identity colour per land tile by owner, run-merged, a 1 px frontier line ONLY between horizontally adjacent runs (north-south borders between rows are never drawn), a year stamp. No terrain, no rivers, no seats, no roads. Twelve identity colours cover 24-60 powers, so three to five polities share a colour and a fragmentation into same-coloured successors can be invisible.

THE WORK. (1) Lift the landform and river rasters into ui::history_lapse beside the packed land raster it already carries (the wizard has the generated tiles; river_edges and terrain_landform are per-tile facts). (2) Draw a dull terrain base -- relief for mountain/highland/canyon/rift, a river stroke along river edges -- and draw the culture or polity fill as a translucent tint over it. (3) Draw the frontier on both axes. (4) Draw each polity's seat as a dot (the in-game Ages view already draws one dot per region; here it is seats only, so blob granularity is legible). (5) Colour adjacent polities distinctly: assign colours at record time by a greedy colouring over the neighbour graph rather than hashing the id, so no two neighbours share a hue; kin cultures share a hue family per BL-919.

BOUND. ImGui 16-bit draw indices cap the run-merged rect count (~1,000 per frame today); the terrain base is static per round and can be baked once into a texture or a cached draw list rather than re-merged per frame.

DONE WHEN: a headless capture of round 4 at three years across the span shows rivers, relief, seats and closed frontiers under a tinted fill; no two adjacent polities share a colour in the capture; a live click confirms the map still animates at frame rate.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The record carries typed events, the round shows them as they happen, and the arc readout counts what actually happened
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: the moments of the arc -- cultures breaking into insular groups, polities breaking back into city states, empires forming and falling -- "are not outcomes for the end, but part of the time-lapse." CIVILISATION.md sec The arc is watched, not read off at the end.

WHAT THE RECORD CARRIES TODAY. era_timelapse = owner_change{year, region, owner} on change, polity_sample per 20-year step, culture_change deltas, corridors with no year. A secession is pushed as ordinary owner_changes to a fresh polity id with no cause field, so on the map a break-away is a colour flip indistinguishable from a conquest. Extinction, capital moves, creed adoption, civilisation formation and culture splits are counters or prose lines in out.history that reach only the in-game Story view. struct polity has no name and no parent field.

TWO READOUT DEFECTS RIDE ON THIS. summarise_lapse_arc counts a polity as destroyed when its last sample holds zero regions, but record_step samples LIVING polities only, so "destroyed" is structurally 0 on every world (the BL-891 capture's "0 destroyed" was an artefact; the sweep shows powers falling in 31 of 32 worlds). And peak share divides by the FINAL region stride while the region count grows four to six times inside the run, so an early empire reads a quarter of its true share. Both are fixed here by reading the event list.

THE WORK. (1) A typed event list on era_timelapse: {year, kind, region, polity, other} with kinds for founded, seat captured, realm ended (other = killer), broke away (other = parent), capital moved, road promoted, civilisation formed, creed preached, and in round 3 culture split (other = parent culture). (2) polity gains a parent field so a successor can be named "X, broken from Y" (the lineage that today survives only as a ground_taken grudge). (3) The sim emits at the sites that already push prose. (4) Save-format bump (12 -> 13); the roundtrip check pins a literal. (5) In the wizard: an event ticker in the left column, a marker pulsing at the event's region for about a screen-second, the arc readout recomputed from events with a live-stride denominator, and the board's Population and Might columns drawn from the polity_sample series that already carries them (the "in flight" seam note in history_lapse.cpp is stale, BL-817 is complete). (6) Harness: bounds on the event list as B817b bounds playback (< 1 MB), and recorded-vs-suppressed bit-identity.

DONE WHEN: a capture of round 4 shows a "breaks away" and a "realm ended" line in the ticker with a marker on the map; the arc readout's destroyed count matches the sweep's gross deaths on the same seed; save_roundtrip is green at version 13; world_determinism unchanged.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: Roads grow on the Empires map as they are walked, and a road over a river is a bridge
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: the round should show polities "rendering roads and bridges across rivers". CIVILISATION.md calls the road the empire's skeleton; today the skeleton is invisible on the one surface that shows its consequences.

WHAT EXISTS. Corridors are recorded (era_timelapse history_corridor{a, b, uses}) with counts and NO year, so the network cannot be animated; ~50 corridors per world are promoted to Track or Road, ~1,600 are walked once. Surviving corridors are stamped as road tiles on the campaign map by road_generation.cpp, so the campaign sees them and the wizard never does. Rivers are on tiles (river_edges) and the migration walk prices them; the Empires sim reads no river anywhere.

THE WORK. BL-916's road_promoted event carries the year a corridor crosses a tier, so the lapse draws the promoted network as it forms: a faint stroke on first promotion, heavier at Road. A corridor segment that crosses a river edge draws a bridge glyph at the crossing -- a pure render fact, no sim change. Walked-once corridors are NOT drawn (the settle tree is dense and mostly one-use; drawing it would be plaid).

DONE WHEN: a late-span capture of round 4 shows the promoted network over the terrain base with bridge glyphs at river crossings, and an early-span capture shows almost none of it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The migration coins many kin cultures, a range breaks into insular groups, and the round shows it happening
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "ensure that different biomes cause cultural rifts... I would prefer to see many cultures that are similar, rather than one big culture... Having an extremely diverse cultural set can only be beneficial. If you need to over-tune splits - I encourage that." Written into COLONISATION.md sec Diversity is the deliverable.

WHAT EXISTS. Two split triggers in colonisation.cpp: a lineage may diverge once per colonisation_split_centiyears (600 years) as its stream walks, and settling ground of a different farm class than the class it was coined on (BL-864) coins a daughter -- at most ONCE per class per lineage, a bound added after an unbounded first cut coined 1,739 peoples on one world. Daughters inherit pantheon and tongue (creeds.hpp); kinship is years to the common ancestor. Seeds 0 and 1 already carry 676 and 929 cultures with a tree depth of 9-10 -- so the count is not the problem; what is missing is (a) a split that happens AFTER settlement, so a culture spread over a range can come apart, and (b) a face that reports the shape.

THE WORK. (1) Loosen the walk triggers toward diversity: shorter split interval, the biome trigger firing on every class transition rather than once per class per lineage, with the 1,739 runaway as the ceiling to stay under, not a target. (2) The ISOLATION trigger, the mechanism behind "a range breaking down into insular groups": at each record step, a culture's settled regions are partitioned into components over cheap-traversal adjacency (a mountain, a strait, sheer distance breaks a component); a component cut off from the culture's origin component for longer than a divergence span coins a daughter on that component. Deterministic -- a consequence of terrain and time, never a roll; iteration in region-index order. Which round it runs in is a call on the form (NR-839): round 3 only, or both. (3) Each split emits BL-916's culture_split event so the round-3 lapse shows a lobe changing hue as it diverges. (4) Measure: cultures per world, tree depth, mean kinship of adjacent cultures, and the share of splits by trigger, printed by the colonisation harness and carried on the sweep's JSON row -- "over-tune" is only honest against a number.

DONE WHEN: a headless capture of round 3 at three years shows a range coming apart into kin hues; the sweep face prints cultures per world and the split census; no seed reaches the 1,739 runaway; world_determinism unchanged.

RULED 2026-09-11 (Ben, form, NR-839): the isolation split runs in the CULTURE ROUND ONLY. The Empires phase does not coin cultures by isolation; it merges and mixes.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: Kin cultures share a hue family, so many similar cultures read as families rather than noise
items.design:
The consequence of BL-918 for the map: hundreds of cultures under twelve identity colours is plaid. A daughter must look like its parent's kin.

THE RULE. Hue comes from the root cradle; a daughter takes its parent's hue shifted a fixed step around the wheel and a lightness step by depth, so siblings are distinguishable and a family is recognisable at a glance. Round 3 draws culture ground in these hues. In round 4 the same hue family tints the dull culture base beneath the polity fill (BL-915), so a war that takes a whole culture reads as one family being swallowed.

DONE WHEN: a round-3 capture shows visibly related hues along a migration route and a clearly different family on another cradle's ground; the palette is derived from the culture tree at record time and needs no per-frame work.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The Empires phase opens on culture ground, and city states rise by organising it
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "We should reframe this as something that lives on top of culture. Initially, we should see a dull version of the culture map, with city-states rising and gaining control of provinces, setting up trade with amicable neighbours... and beginning to start wars that conquer entire cultures - causing a cultural merge. What we currently see is the same few powers consolidating and battling over neighbour provinces, continually changing hands. I believe that the solution will be this prior change to culture, where there is room for some select powerhouses to clearly grow." CIVILISATION.md sec The arc is watched, not read off at the end.

WHAT THE OPENING IS TODAY (history_sim.cpp seeding). One polity per plurality culture present in the opening region set, holding EVERY region of that culture -- 24 to 60 culture-blobs of ~4.5 regions, never a field of city states. Every scheduled founding after 400 BCE (the BL-846 schedule, 3-6x the opening count over the span) is handed to the incumbent polity of its culture with no verb and no contest, so a polity's size at 1200 CE tracks how far its people walked, not how it acted. Taking a seat takes every region pointing at it; a city state dies in one battle and a big realm loses a whole bloc. CIVILISATION.md sec The unit is the city state describes an opening the code does not produce.

THE REFRAME. (1) The opening: culture ground is peopled and UNORGANISED; a city state is a seat that has organised some of it. How many city states open the phase is NR-835's call (one per culture at its best region, or every opening region). (2) A polity grows over unorganised ground by an ORGANISE verb: reach-gated (BL-922 -- the network must supply the ground), priced by kinship (own culture cheapest, kin dearer, opposed peoples cannot be organised, only conquered). This is the growth that gives a powerhouse room, and it turns the kin discount that today makes kin ground HARDER to take (w_cult scaled by opposition) into the path of cheap growth, while opposition still permits conquest of strangers. (3) Scheduled foundings arrive as unorganised ground of their culture, not as free hinterland -- incumbents stop growing for free. (4) A hinterland region points at the nearest seat, and a centre that grows on unorganised ground becomes a new city state, so city states keep RISING through the span. (5) The map draws unorganised ground as the dull culture tint (BL-915/919) and organised ground in the polity's colour, so growth is literally visible as colour spreading over the base.

NOT CHANGED. Ground is never released to nobody by collapse (CIVILISATION.md sec What the dark age must leave); unorganised ground exists only as the opening condition and as foundings arrive. Conquest, cohesion, assimilation and the closure contract stand.

DONE WHEN: the round-4 capture at 400 BCE shows a dull culture map with a few bright seats; by mid-span colour has spread over most of the base; the sweep prints city-state count over time and the share of ground organised vs conquered; largest share and rise count are read before and after with no target set.

RULED 2026-09-11 (Ben, form, NR-835, Other): "City states spawn in provinces above a threshold population. Choose a sensible number - your judgement will be good here." THE OPENING RULE: a region whose population is above the city-state threshold is a city state -- at 400 BCE and whenever it crosses the line later -- and everything else is unorganised culture ground. No one-per-culture rule, no every-region rule. THE NUMBER, chosen as asked: 300,000 heads, provisional. The reasoning: carrying capacity is 5,000 + 500 x farm_q (settlement.cpp region_carrying_capacity) and the mean end-of-span region holds ~230,000, so 300,000 selects the better-farmed third or so of the regions standing at 400 BCE, which are old enough to sit at their ceiling; later foundings open at 2,000-26,000 and grow toward their ceiling over about three centuries, so city states keep rising through the span at the rate the ground fills. BL-926's census prints the opening distribution; the build reads the share the threshold selects and adjusts the number only to keep that intent (a minority at the opening, a steady rise after), recording the value it ships. Never a target, never a quota per world.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: An attack draws on the realm its network can supply, so a large realm fights a larger battle
items.design:
THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE OF NO COMPOUNDING, found by the 2026-09-11 holistic read and stated by no earlier item. gather_army (history_sim.cpp) = the staging hub's own garrison plus at most the same again from HALF of adjacent held garrisons; every garrison converges yearly to garrison_target = 40% of manpower = 2% of its own region's population (settlement.cpp muster_garrison). The defender levies from the same local pool. So a 150-region empire and a 3-region polity fight the same-sized battle at any border, and p_win = atk/(atk+def) is a function of two regions' farm_q, not of who rules them. This is why every brake on a riser measured null (BL-838, BL-839, BL-887, BL-905): there is no riser, because success writes nothing into force.

BEN, 2026-09-11: "before this we must ensure we can see strong growth - as the current levers paint a more stable picture than I want to see."

THE SHAPE. Force follows the network: a campaign's stack is gathered from every held region the staging hub can reach along the supplied network, each contributing a share of its garrison weighted by its network_supply_q (BL-922's gradient) and by road hops -- so a realm with roads brings more of itself to a border than one without, and reach is finally the lever the design says it is (the wall moves when you win). Whether a standing field army bought from seat stock sits beside this is NR-836's call. The defender's emergency levy stays local. Upkeep already prices heads (BL-895), so a bigger stack costs more to keep. Systemic and legible: the force has a visible cause on the map -- the roads and the ground behind them.

DONE WHEN: on the sweep, p_win at a border rises with the attacker's supplied region count; largest share and the count of polities that rise move materially from the BL-907 baseline (no target set); a fixture with a 3-region and a 30-region polity at one border shows the larger stack; world_determinism unchanged.

RULED 2026-09-11 (Ben, form, NR-836): A -- the POOLED LEVY along the supplied network. No standing field army in this sprint. The levy is priced from the capital (NR-838): a region contributes in proportion to its network_supply_q read from the capital, over held ground, discounted by roads.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: Supply is priced from the seat over the ground a realm holds, at a cost that makes distance matter
items.design:
ANSWERS BL-905's OWED CALL ("whether/how to redesign the reach-gate currency") and the reason BL-896's secession fires only on islands.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY (history_sim.cpp rebuild_reach / network_supply_q). Reach is one Dijkstra per polity from its capital over the WHOLE region graph, ownership-blind: a realm's seat reaches its far block through foreign-held ground at the same cost, so "a war that emptied the ground between" -- one of the four causes CIVILISATION.md names for a fragmentation -- is not a mechanism as built. network_supply_q = 1000 - reach x terrain_reach_cost_q(10)/100, i.e. 0.1 supply per plains tile; the longest connected path on the map loses ~30 of 1,000, so every connected region reads 970-1000 and the floors (settlement 40, secession 60, garrison 0) are reachable only by ground in a different connected component. The harness fixtures that make the floors bite set terrain_reach_cost_q 26x to 2,500x the shipped value. campaign_supply prices hub-to-target distance capped at 9 tiles, which is why the campaign gate is a step function (BL-905).

THE CALL (NR-838, form). Recommended: price network_supply_q from the seat over HELD ground only, with a per-tile cost rescaled so that ordinary distant ground reads materially lower; roads discount it (Ben's 2026-09-10 ruling: the wall moves when you win, geography must be BUILT past). campaign_supply shares the basis so the reach gate refuses a real share rather than 0 or 94%. Sea legs and the water gate stand.

WHAT MUST STAY TRUE. Deterministic, integer, replayable; the digest changes (a new supply field means new decisions) and world_determinism re-blesses once, as a wave act. The magnitude is measured, not chosen: print the distribution of network_supply_q over held regions and the share under each floor before and after.

DONE WHEN: a connected region 30+ tiles from its seat reads materially below one beside it; the sweep's "REFUSED reach gate" is neither 0 nor nearly everything; secession candidates exist on connected ground; world_determinism green after one authorised re-bless.

RULED 2026-09-11 (Ben, form, NR-838): "Price in that polity's capital. In the Empire phase, each polity sees itself as the strategic headquarters where any supply, or material gain is stockpiled." THE CAPITAL IS THE BASIS FOR EVERYTHING: network_supply_q (holding, growth, breakdown), campaign_supply (the gate and the battle), the levy (BL-921) and the stockpile (material_stock lives at the capital, not at every seat -- a captured seat's stock is carried home). The staging-hub pricing goes. The traversal domain is HELD ground only (decision taken on Ben's behalf, recorded on NR-838): foreign ground is impassable to supply, so a war that takes the ground between a capital and its far block cuts the block off. Rescale the per-tile cost so ordinary distant ground reads materially lower and the floors bite on connected ground; print the supply distribution before and after; one authorised re-bless of world_determinism.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: A realm that has spread too far breaks back down into city states, and the round shows it
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "polities which have spread too far also breaking back down into city states... not outcomes for the end, but part of the time-lapse."

WHAT EXISTS (BL-896). Ground whose network_supply_q falls under 60 secedes as a contiguous block of at least two regions into ONE successor that copies the parent's ladders and cohesion; NR-826 call 2 set the block floor deliberately so a realm SPLITS rather than SHATTERS into specks. Measured median 2 secessions and 14 regions per world, unchanged from 400 to 1,600 years, all on graph-disconnected ground. A successor is named by its seat and carries no lineage.

THE CHANGE. Ground the seat can no longer supply breaks into CITY STATES: each cut-off seat, with the hinterland pointing at it, becomes its own polity; a cut-off region with no seat joins the nearest cut-off seat or becomes a city state of its own. Each successor records its parent (BL-916), emits a broke-away event, takes its seat's plurality culture (NR-826 call 3 stands), and a ground_taken grudge is raised. The parent loses cohesion through the ordinary channel. A successor can itself fragment later; it is exempt only in its birth round. NR-837 (form) is the call on the unit: city states (reverses NR-826 call 2) or blocks of two or more.

MECHANICAL, NEVER SCHEDULED. No collapse fires on a date; the cause stays what CIVILISATION.md sec How an empire actually falls names -- distance, terrain, a road never built, a war that emptied the ground between -- which BL-922 makes true of connected ground for the first time. Ground is never released to nobody.

DONE WHEN: across the sweep, breakdowns occur on connected ground and the pieces are city-state sized; the sweep prints breakdowns, pieces and piece sizes per world; a round-4 capture shows a realm coming apart with "breaks away" lines in the ticker; a peaceable seed stays legitimate.

RULED 2026-09-11 (Ben, form, NR-837): A -- CITY STATES, ONE PER CUT-OFF SEAT. NR-826 call 2 (blocks of two or more) is reversed; call 3 (the successor takes its seat's plurality culture) stands. A cut-off region with no seat joins the nearest cut-off seat, and where there is none it stands alone as a city state of its own -- it is never handed to a neighbour and never released to nobody (the dark-age ruling stands: collapse does not re-wild). The cut is read from the capital (NR-838).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: A region is worth attacking for what stands on it, so wars drive on cities instead of trading border ground
items.design:
THE FINDING. region_value_q = (farm + ore + port)/3 -- static endowment. Population, centres, urban population, works and seat status play no part in what a region is worth to attack, so no capital is worth more than a hamlet and campaign targeting has no gradient toward a decisive objective. The 4-seed sweep at full span shows the consequence: 168 regions ever conquered per world against 1,728 conquests, 28% of contested regions taken three or more times, 12.9 changes per contested region, the worst 242 times -- border churn that logs conquests without moving the political map. Ben's read of the live round ("the same few powers... battling over neighbour provinces, continually changing hands") is this number.

THE CHANGE. Region value reads the centres standing on it and whether it is a seat, so a city is a prize and a seat is the prize; the scorer already prices defence and works, so a rich seat is also a hard one. Sacking a seat already razes centres, so a taken city is worth less to retake -- the churn cools by itself.

DONE WHEN: the sweep's share of conquests that are seats rises and "TAKEN 3+ TIMES" falls from the 4-seed baseline (28%), no target set; determinism unchanged.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: Amicable neighbours trade across their border, and the round draws the link
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: city states "setting up trade with amicable neighbours".

WHAT EXISTS (BL-895). Trade income is paid only INSIDE a realm: for a pair of same-owner neighbouring regions joined by a walked corridor whose trade class differs, the seat earns trade_income_per_link a year. Nothing crosses a border, so "amicable" has no meaning in the sim, and trade is 0.25% of production (NR-827).

THE RULE. Two neighbouring polities are amicable when their cultures are kin (opposition below the civilisation bar) and neither holds a biting grudge against the other. A walked corridor joining unlike ground across an amicable border pays both seats, at BL-895's constant; a grudge raised on either side closes the link until it decays. No market, no price -- the no-market ruling stands. The lapse draws an open link as a stroke between the two seats (BL-917's corridor draw), so "trading with amicable neighbours" is visible.

DONE WHEN: the sweep prints cross-border links open per world and trade's share of production before and after; a round-4 capture shows links between kin seats and none across a border with a live grudge.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The instrument reports the arc as lifespans, deaths, pieces and cultures, and the JSON carries them
items.design:
MEASURE BEFORE RESHAPING. Every sprint-39 mechanism is judged by a before/after read, and the instrument cannot see most of what this sprint is about.

NOT MEASURED TODAY: per-polity death year and GROSS deaths (only powers_end < powers_start, which nets births against deaths -- seed 0 shows 27 polities dead against a reported net loss of 9); successor lineage and secession piece sizes (only a total); how long an empire held its peak; the distribution of network_supply_q over held regions and the share at 0 (disconnected) or under each floor; cultures per world, tree depth and adjacent-culture kinship; the share of foundings from the schedule vs the Settle verb; city-state count over time; civilisations formed. The JSON row carries 20 of ~90 fields, none of the funnel, churn, secession, creed or fear figures, so no two runs can be diffed off disk.

THE WORK. Add the readings above to the report face and to the JSON row; a per-polity table (born, peak, peak year, died, killer or parent) printed for the top N; the supply histogram; the culture census. Also print the arc mode on the JSON so a row says which span it measured. Do this FIRST in the batch so every later item has its baseline.

DONE WHEN: the 16-seed sweep on main before any other sprint-39 item lands is saved as the baseline; every field above is on the face and in the row.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: The creed-aggression lean is applied once per candidate, not once per season
items.design:
NR-831 (open observation). w_aggr_q's lean sits INSIDE the two-season loop in the campaign scorer, so the winter pass re-leans the already-leaned summer value: at generation's w_aggr_q = 300 a warlike people is pushed x1.30 in summer and x1.69 in winter, a placid one x0.70 and x0.49. The fear lean beside it is deliberately applied once, outside the loop, with a comment stating that as the rule. BL-868's delivered magnitude includes this unwritten squaring.

THE FIX. Apply the lean once, outside the season loop, matching the fear lean's siting; re-read the sweep's battle and conquest medians; record the before/after beside NR-831. Light, one file.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 design session); Claude (filed from the holistic generation read)
items.title: A river and a mountain defend, in the resolver and in the scorer that chooses the fight
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "I would argue we also need a deeper combat system, so that we take into account defence over rivers and mountains, but before this we must ensure we can see strong growth." DEFERRED BY THAT RULING: no sprint until sprint 39's growth items have landed and been read.

WHAT EXISTS. resolve_battle carries a landform defence multiplier on the defender only (mountain strongest, then rift, canyon, crater, highland, valley) and a doctrine mountain_penalty. The campaign scorer never sees the terrain term (battle_trace's own comment: "the term the scorer never sees"), so attackers do not avoid mountains, they lose there. Rivers are absent from the resolver and from the Empires sim entirely; only the migration walk reads them.

DESIGN OWED. Whether a river is a defence term on the region behind it or a crossing cost on the corridor; whether the scorer reads terrain so a campaign routes around a range or over a bridge (BL-917 draws bridges; this is what would make them matter); how it composes with works defence. Written against MILITARY_HISTORY.md sec The resolver when taken up.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, sprint-39 form, further detail); Claude (filed)
items.title: A polity spends the stockpile at its capital on upgrading supply sites, so trade and conquest buy reach
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11 (form, further detail): "a polity should be able to upgrade supply sites spending our stockpiled 'industry points' gained through trade or conquest." And on the basis: "each polity sees itself as the strategic headquarters where any supply, or material gain is stockpiled." His 'industry points' are this project's MATERIALS (CIVILISATION.md sec What materials are FOR); the stockpile is material_stock at the capital.

WHAT EXISTS. The build_work verb (BL-321) raises an Era -1 work on the capital or one hash-rotated holding, scored by work_score_q with a reach weight (w_work_reach 1200), and it "never wins the scored contest" per its own comment; works cost materials to build (BL-895) and a reach work relieves terrain cost on its region (work_reach_relief_cap_q). Corridor promotion also costs the seat (road_build_material_cost 2000) but is triggered by USE, not by choice. A captured seat carries its stock to the winner (BL-867); trade pays the seat (BL-895, BL-925). So the pieces exist and none of them is a deliberate spend on the network's weak link.

THE SHAPE. A SUPPLY SITE is a held region's reach work, or a corridor's tier, upgraded by choice: the scorer offers "upgrade the supply site at X" as a candidate wherever a held region's network_supply_q (from the capital, BL-922) is low or falling, priced from the capital's stockpile, and prefers the site that lifts the most held ground above the floors. Trade (BL-925) and conquest (a captured seat's stock carried home) are what fill the stockpile, so a realm that trades and wins can afford to reach further -- the wall moves when you win, paid for. A realm that cannot pay watches its far ground break away (BL-923). Deterministic integer scorer, fixed tie-break, no floats.

RENDER. An upgraded site draws on the lapse (BL-915/917): a waystation glyph on the region, a heavier road stroke on the corridor.

DONE WHEN: the sweep prints supply-site upgrades per world and materials spent on them beside upkeep, roads and campaigns; realms with higher trade income upgrade more sites (read, not targeted); a round-4 capture shows waystations along a realm's roads; determinism unchanged.
